replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I have a neutral relationship with mathematics. It's not my favorite subject, but I understand its importance in my daily life and work. I use basic math for budgeting and managing my self-employed business, but I don't delve into complex topics.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I don't get anxious about basic math, but complex topics like calculus or algebra can make me feel a bit overwhelmed. I prefer to stick to what I know and understand.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used an AI math tutor last year to brush up on some basic algebra. It was a positive experience. The AI was patient and allowed me to learn at my own pace.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real roots. If Δ = 0, there's one real root. If Δ < 0, there are no real roots. Finally, use the quadratic formula (x = [-b ± √(Δ)] / (2a)) to find the roots.

To find stationary points, first find the derivative of the function (f'(x)). Then, set the derivative equal to zero (f'(x) = 0) and solve for x. These x-values are the stationary points. To determine if they're maxima or minima, find the second derivative (f''(x)) and evaluate it at the stationary points. If f''(x) > 0, it's a minimum. If f''(x) < 0, it's a maximum.
